items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The records included stuff by Jelly Roll Morton, stuff by Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson.

ctx.x: Well I’ve noticed that one thing that we’ve been interested in here in doing these archival tapes is that we keep some of the earlier jazz stories and music alive for students and anyone watching. And it seems to be kind of a passion of yours that the early, some of the early keyboard styles. Is this something that you’ve liked from the beginning? Or did you come to it later on?

I liked it from the beginning, and the beginning for me really was a large collection of 78 RPM records which my big brother had collected and left to me when he went off to college. That really was my basic education. The records included stuff by Jelly Roll © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Morton, stuff by Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson. And although I didn’t like it much at first, even stuff by Zez Confrey and ragtime people like that, novelty piano people like that. But I never thought that I would be using that background in my professional career. It never seemed that there was any reason to expect that. But at a certain point it did happen and I brushed off what I remembered from all that and got involved in Scott Joplin specifically and Jelly Roll Morton and it came in very handy. And I really…
